subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory full reindexing gain a durable checkpoint/resume model now, and if so should it be default-only or exposed through memorySearch config/status controls?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix changes durable memory generation state, search/status semantics, and possibly public configuration, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Design resumable generations
options.body: Implement a durable generation/checkpoint model in the memory-core SQLite path, with search/status guarding incomplete generations and focused crash/resume regression coverage.

options.title: Keep only adjacent hardening
options.body: Continue landing narrower metadata, WAL, lock, and cleanup repairs while leaving long-running checkpoint/resume as a later product design.

options.title: Decline configurable resume
options.body: Reject the new config surface and document that forced full reindex remains all-or-nothing, relying on smaller paths and provider reliability instead.

recommendation.title: Design resumable generations
recommendation.body: Implement a durable generation/checkpoint model in the memory-core SQLite path, with search/status guarding incomplete generations and focused crash/resume regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent live history shows vincentkoc has carried the central memory DB/reindex safety changes most closely tied to this decision.
